fixtures.governing_table: Table AC-403.1 of Article XV of the Allegheny County Health Department Rules and Regulations governs toilet counts in Pittsburgh, with Section 403.1.1 (half men, half women, fractions round up), Section AC-403.2 (separate rooms) and Section AC-424.2 (urinals). The state plumbing code's Table 403.1 is not enforced in Allegheny County (34 Pa. Code 403.21(a)(6)); the county's code must meet the state minimum, and its counts for offices, restaurants and schools are equal to or higher than the state table's at every size worked. The same state table also sits in Chapter 29 of the building code (Table 2902.1), which is adopted statewide with no county exception; PLI says it does not enforce plumbing code provisions and that the county has sole authority over them, so the county table is the one applied on plumbing permits. Footnote 21 of the county table itself refers to the state table as the lower figure. The amendment is the county's, not the city's: the city has no toilet-count table of its own.

amendment.text: Allegheny County's own table. Per sex (half the occupants each): Business (offices): 1 toilet for 1 to 15 people, 2 for 16 to 35, 3 for 36 to 55, 4 for 56 to 80, 5 for 81 to 110, 6 for 111 to 150, then 1 more per 40. Restaurants, bars and similar (A-2): men 2 for 1 to 50, 3 for 51 to 100, 4 for 101 to 160, then 1 more per 40; women 1 for 1 to 25, 2 for 26 to 50, 3 for 51 to 100, 4 for 101 to 160, then 1 more per 40. Schools: elementary students 1 per 40 male and 1 per 30 female; the 'Elementary (secondary)' and 'University, adult centers, etc.' rows 1 per 50 male and 1 per 40 female; staff as offices. Urinals are required: at least 50% of the men's required toilets, and toilets may be reduced by the urinals used but not below 50% of the tabulated number. In restaurants and bars a single-occupancy restroom needs a urinal (family restrooms excepted), and 8 or more toilets in total trigger a required single-user toilet room. Separate rooms are not required at 15 occupants or fewer in total (business: 15 or fewer; mercantile: 50 or fewer).
amendment.quote: TABLE AC-403.1 MINIMUM NUMBER OF REQUIRED PLUMBING FIXTURES (See Sections 403.1.1 and 403.2). A-2 | Nightclubs, bars, taverns, dance halls, and buildings for similar purposes, restaurants, banquet halls, and food courts | WATER CLOSETS MALE: 2 per 1-50; 3 per 51-100; 4 per 101-160; over 160, add 1 per 40 | FEMALE: 1 per 25; 2 per 26-50; 3 per 51-100; 4 per 101-160; over 160, add 1 per 40 | footnotes 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. B | Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, light industrial and similar uses | MALE and FEMALE each: 1 per 1-15; 2 per 16-35; 3 per 36-55; 4 per 56-80; 5 per 81-110; 6 per 111-150; over 150, add 1 per 40. E | Elementary (students): MALE 1 per 40, FEMALE 1 per 30 | Elementary (secondary): MALE 1 per 50, FEMALE 1 per 40 | University, adult centers, etc.: MALE 1 per 50, FEMALE 1 per 40 | Staff (all schools): same as office buildings. Footnote 13: In A-2 occupancy, urinals are required in single occupancy bathrooms (does not include family bathrooms). Footnote 14: In A-2 occupancy, when the aggregate of 8 or more male and female water closets are provided, a single-user toilet room, including family assisted or assisted use bathroom, is required. Footnote 21: If the minimum number of required plumbing fixtures for an occupancy under Table 403.1 exceeds the minimum number of required plumbing fixtures under Table 403.1 of the International Plumbing Code promulgated by the Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry, then the additional plumbing fixtures may be located in single-user toilet and bathing room(s) [...] (Ordinance 11-22-OR, Exhibit A, pages 13 to 20) | 403.2 exception 2: Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or less. (Ordinance 11-22-OR) | exception 4: Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 15 or fewer. (Ordinance 31-22-OR) | UpCodes copy: 403.1.1 Fixture Calculations. To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. To determine the required number of fixtures, the fixture ratio or ratios for each fixture type shall be applied to the occupant load of each sex in accordance with Table AC-403.1. Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table AC-403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. | AC-424.2 Number of Urinals. The number of urinals for males shall be at least 50% of the total number of water closets required for males. The number of water closets may be decreased by the number of urinals which are used, but the number of remaining water closets shall not be less than 50% of the original tabulated total. | AC-310.4 Water Closet Compartment. Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. | AC-310.5 Urinal Partitions. Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy. [...] Exceptions: Urinal partitions shall not be required in a single occupant or family/assisted-use toilet room with a lockable door.

worked_examples.how: 50/2 = 25 per sex. Business row: '2 per 16-35', so 2 each. Men: urinals at least 50% of 2 = 1; toilets may drop by the urinals used but not below 50% of 2 = 1. So 1 stall + 1 urinal.

100/2 = 50 per sex. '3 per 36-55', so 3 each. Men: urinals at least 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 2; remaining toilets not less than 1.5, so 2. So 2 stalls + 2 urinals (literal reading; the rule does not say how an odd number splits).
200/2 = 100 per sex. '5 per 81-110', so 5 each. Men: urinals at least 2.5, so 3; toilets not less than 2.5, so 3. So 3 stalls + 3 urinals (literal reading).
400/2 = 200 per sex. '6 per 111-150', then 'over 150, add 1 per 40': 50 over, 50/40 = 1.25, rounds up to 2; 6 + 2 = 8 each. Men: 4 urinals, 4 stalls.
50/2 = 25 per sex. A-2 row. Female: '1 per 1-25' (the ordinance prints '1 per 25'), so 1. Male: '2 per 1-50', so 2. Men: urinals at least 1, toilets not less than 1. So 1 stall + 1 urinal.
100/2 = 50 per sex. Female: '2 per 26-50', so 2. Male: '2 per 1-50', so 2: 1 stall + 1 urinal.

200/2 = 100 per sex. '3 per 51-100' for each sex, so 3 each. Men: urinals at least 1.5, so 2; toilets not less than 1.5, so 2 (literal reading). Aggregate toilets 6, below the 8 that triggers footnote 14.

400/2 = 200 per sex. '4 per 101-160', then 'over 160, add 1 per 40': 40 over, 40/40 = 1; 4 + 1 = 5 each. Men: urinals at least 2.5, so 3; toilets not less than 2.5, so 3 (literal reading). Aggregate toilets 10: footnote 14 requires a single-user toilet room as well.

50/2 = 25 per sex. Male 1 per 40: 25/40 = 0.63, rounds up to 1. Female 1 per 30: 25/30 = 0.83, rounds up to 1. Men: urinals at least 50% of 1 = 0.5, so 1; toilets not less than 0.5, so 1 (literal reading: 1 stall + 1 urinal).
100/2 = 50 per sex. Male 50/40 = 1.25, rounds up to 2. Female 50/30 = 1.67, rounds up to 2. Men: 1 stall + 1 urinal.
200/2 = 100 per sex. Male 100/40 = 2.5, rounds up to 3. Female 100/30 = 3.33, rounds up to 4. Men: urinals at least 1.5, so 2; toilets not less than 1.5, so 2 (literal reading).
400/2 = 200 per sex. Male 200/40 = 5. Female 200/30 = 6.67, rounds up to 7. Men: urinals at least 2.5, so 3; toilets not less than 2.5, so 3 (literal reading).

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Men's side read literally from AC-424.2: urinals are at least half of the tabulated toilets and the remaining toilets are not less than half, each rounded up to a whole fixture. For an odd tabulated number this gives one fixture more than the table (3 becomes 2 stalls + 2 urinals); the rule does not say how to round, and the Plumbing Program may accept another split. School rows use 'Elementary (students)'. With the 'Elementary (secondary)' or 'University' rows (male 1 per 50, female 1 per 40): 50 occupants 1 female / 1 male; 100: 2 / 1; 200: 3 / 2; 400: 5 / 4. The state Restroom Equity rule (two women's toilets per men's toilet or urinal in some public facilities) is not applied here.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Pittsburgh job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see Allegheny County's toilet-count rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Pittsburgh hospitals, university buildings, downtown offices and schools, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** in Pittsburgh the number of toilets and urinals comes from the Allegheny County Health Department's plumbing rules, not from the state plumbing rules used in most of Pennsylvania. The county has its own table and requires urinals in men's rooms. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** the city's Department of Permits, Licenses and Inspections (PLI) issues building permits in Pittsburgh. Its list of work that needs no permit includes ordinary repairs, painting, tiling, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work, and movable partitions no taller than 5 feet 9 inches. Cutting away a wall or partition is not an ordinary repair. The list doesn't name toilet partitions fixed to the floor or wall, so ask PLI (412-255-2175) whether your replacement needs one. Plumbing is the county's: installing, moving or replacing a toilet or urinal needs a plumbing permit from the Allegheny County Health Department's Plumbing Program (412-578-8036). You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and urinals are in stalls or screened from view. Allegheny County's plumbing rules say the same. In a restaurant or bar the county also requires a urinal in a one-person restroom, unless it is a family restroom. We found no Pennsylvania law or Pittsburgh ordinance that limits who may use which restroom.
page.confirm_office: the Pittsburgh Department of Permits, Licenses and Inspections and the Allegheny County Health Department's Plumbing Program
page.stalls_intro: In Pittsburgh the counts come from Allegheny County's plumbing rules. They count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women, and any fraction rounds up. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are required: in the men's room there must be at least half as many urinals as the toilets the county's table asks for, and urinals may take the place of up to half of those toilets. Each urinal needs a screen. The table shows women's stalls, then men's stalls plus urinals.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building. Where the county's table gives the men's side an odd number, half of it isn't a whole number. The table above rounds both the stalls and the urinals up, and the county's rules don't say how to round, so confirm the split with the Plumbing Program (412-578-8036). For secondary schools and universities the county counts one toilet per 50 men and one per 40 women. A space with 15 people or fewer in total doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms. A restaurant or bar with eight or more toilets in total must also have a single-user restroom. A separate Pennsylvania law asks for two women's toilets for every men's toilet or urinal in new or largely rebuilt public middle and high schools, arenas, stadiums and convention halls, so ask your building code official whether it covers your project.
page.install_rule: Pittsburgh requires a City general contractor license for all work done under a commercial building permit, issued by the city's Department of Permits, Licenses and Inspections. Pennsylvania has no state license for commercial installers, and its home improvement registration covers residential work only. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: For work under a commercial building permit, the contractor needs a City of Pittsburgh general contractor license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on projects paid for in whole or in part with public money and costing more than $25,000, school district work included, Pennsylvania law requires at least the wage the state Department of Labor & Industry sets for each trade in the county; maintenance work is not covered. The state issues its rates project by project. On federally funded building work in Allegheny County the carpenter rate is $42.11 an hour plus $23.21 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7% in Pittsburgh: 6% state and 1% Allegheny County.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hospitals and university campuses:** one material and one hardware standard across many buildings, in solid plastic or phenolic for restrooms that are cleaned many times a day.
